summary: Access approved but console permissions not provisioned after Okta issuer domain swap
description:
Issue summary:
Users report that Access Request approvals show as 'Granted' in the Support Console but the target internal service (runbook/console) still returns 403. Happens after the recent Okta issuer domain swap (okta-old.redwood -> okta-new.redwood).

Impact:
- Internal engineers cannot escalate to runbooks or use the console automation tooling after approvals.
- Blocks oncall workflows during testing; affects ~12 engineers across multiple teams.

Environment:
- prod (us-east) - internal console + identity-proxy + okta-new.redwood

Steps to reproduce:
1) Submit Access Request for runbook elevation in Support Console using existing flow.
2) Approver approves the request (shows Granted in UI).
3) Attempt to open runbook — receives 403 with 'missing RBAC grant'.
4) Inspect auth logs on identity-proxy and console-service.

Observed logs/snippets:
- identity-proxy: "ERROR auth: issuer mismatch: token_iss=https://okta-old.redwood/oauth2/default, expected=https://okta-new.redwood/oauth2/default"
- console-service: "RBAC: no matching grants for principal: user:12345 issuer=https://okta-old.redwood"

Notes: This started after the Okta issuer domain migration rolled earlier this week; some tokens/approval links still carry the old issuer in their assertion/redirect flow.
related_confluence_pages: Confluence: Support Console Auth Flow Diagram
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Priya Shah: Reported by SRE oncall after two engineers couldn't escalate. Assigned to Ethan for initial triage.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Ethan Cole: Reproduced in prod. Token issuer mismatch seen in proxy logs. Hypothesis: approval tokens generated before migration still referencing old issuer; console and proxy validate against new issuer only.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Claire Wu (Identity): Confirmed Okta org swap completed; legacy issuer still active for 24h. We thought token exchange would normalize issuer during exchange but logs disagree.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Ethan Cole: Implemented temporary auth-layer allowance to accept old issuer for access-request assertion path. Rolling to prod canary (10%). Monitoring for unintended acceptance of stale tokens.
2026-03-12 12:00 - SRE oncall: Canary at 10% shows successful provisioning for previously-failing users. No obvious regression in other flows after 3h.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Priya Shah: Customer-facing note not required (internal only). Tracking follow-up to rotate any long-lived tokens that may contain old issuer references.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: RBAC grant lookup keys include issuer, so any token with old issuer won't match grants issued under new issuer mapping.
Checked audit logs: Access Request approval events authored at 2026-03-09 23:xx still contain 'iss' set to https://okta-old.redwood. Approvals created after 2026-03-10 02:00 have new issuer.
Identity-proxy currently rejects tokens whose 'iss' does not match configured accepted_issuers list (single value).

Support Console's approval token generator signs a short-lived JWT with an 'iss' claim set to the Okta issuer configured at time of generation. Some queued approvals were created before migration and delivered post-migration.

RBAC datastore keys: grants are indexed by (principal_id, issuer). When issuer changes, previously-created grants are still stored under old issuer namespace; provisioning call attempts to read grants using issuer from assertion.
Attempted local repro by forging approval JWT with old issuer and calling provisioning endpoint — repro'd 403 with same logs as production.
resolution_notes: Short term mitigation: Deployed identity-proxy update to accept both https://okta-new.redwood and https://okta-old.redwood on the access-request/provisioning endpoint only. This allowed in-flight approvals to complete normally without touching global token acceptance.

Medium term fix: Backfilled RBAC grants for recently-approved requests by running migration job that normalizes grant keys from old issuer to new issuer for approvals in the migration window (2026-03-09 22:00 -> 2026-03-10 04:00). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-tools/pull/57

Long term: Update approval token generation to include an 'orig_iss' claim and update provisioning to canonicalize issuer during lookup. Add explicit migration step to retirement playbook for future issuer changes. Added unit tests for multi-issuer acceptance in identity-proxy.

Follow-ups:
- Security to review acceptance window (Ethan & Claire).
- Rotate any long-lived service tokens that may embed old issuer references.
- Run additional audit to ensure no external tokens accepted accidentally.
